ROCKET fix, user-reported ("rocket isnt always in the right direction" / flame animation / nose angle). Root cause measured, not guessed: the exported asset's NOSE is drawn +28.33 deg clockwise from straight-up, but the trajectory maths did atan2(dy,dx)+90, which aims a NOSE-UP sprite. So the rocket flew ~28 deg off its own curve for the whole round. Nose offset measured two independent ways that agree - principal-axis analysis of the raster export gives +28.3, and of the SVG as Chrome rasterises it +28.33. Introduced ROCKET_NOSE_OFFSET_DEG and subtracted it from the live angle, and derived the pre-flight pose from it too (the three hardcoded 86 deg resets were also written for a nose-up sprite). VERIFIED in Chrome during a genuine betting-to-flying transition: rendered nose bearing 86.38 deg vs actual travel bearing 85.98 deg over 784px = 0.40 deg ALIGNED (an earlier 8.5 deg reading was a short-sample chord-vs-tangent artifact on a convex path, not a defect). FLAME: the asset BAKES IN its own flame (4189 warm px of a 26402 px render), so the previous three CSS cones were a SECOND differently-coloured flame drawn on top of the design's, positioned as if the nose pointed up. Replaced by layering the same asset twice, each clipped to one side of a line perpendicular to the nose axis at the flame's 97th percentile - hull rigid, the DESIGNER's flame flickering from the nozzle, plus one warm engine glow since a static export cannot itself glow. Flame scale origin resolves to 8.82px/70.32px of the 45x80 box = 19.6% / 87.9%, exactly the measured nozzle. Flame confirmed animating (6-7 distinct transforms per sample run). Build exit 0, tsc clean for AviatorGamePro. Caveat: the numbers are the evidence here - repeated attempts to READ the side-by-side comparison sheet returned "image not available" on this box, so the final aesthetic judgement is unconfirmed by eye and worth a human glance.

ROCKET geometry triad closed. (1) nose-vs-travel 0.40 deg over 784px of real flight; (2) flame-vs-nose bearing 278.09 vs expected 266.38 = 11.71 deg off perfectly-aft, i.e. the flame exits the BACK of the hull as it must - some of that residual is the hull centroid being pulled by the crop's background gradient rather than real misalignment; (3) flame animating, 6-7 distinct transforms per sample run. Pixel census of a tight 286x262 DOM-box crop: 823 warm flame px clustered aft + 4248 hull px, the ratio a correct rocket gives. Note on method: after the curve was corrected to the frame's warm #F77261 gradient, a warm-pixel detector NO LONGER isolates the rocket - it matched the whole curve (bbox spanning x114-1422), so the rocket must be located by its DOM bounding box instead. Also: repeated attempts to READ the comparison sheet returned "image not available" on this box, so the aesthetic call (flicker rate, glow intensity in motion) is unconfirmed by eye and worth a human glance; the geometry above is numeric and does not depend on that read.

ROCKET re-verified by WATCHING THE WHOLE FLIGHT, which CORRECTS my earlier "0.40 deg aligned" claim - that was measured against SCREEN TRAVEL at a single instant, and travel is the wrong reference: logMax is log(max(m,1.16)), so once m>1.16 xProgress=log(m)/log(m)=1 and x PINS at 88% while the graph rescales, i.e. the rocket rises vertically though the curve it draws stays diagonal. I sampled at m=1.05, the one moment before that clamp engages. Watching every frame against the CURVE'S OWN TANGENT exposed two real defects. (1) PROGRESSIVE DRIFT: the angle used a centred chord m*0.98..m*1.02, but the forward sample lands PAST the x-clamp and contributes no dx, so the slope came from a half-truncated chord - error grew to -20.4 deg by 2.5x, increasingly nose-up versus its own curve. Fixed with a BACKWARD chord ending at m, which never crosses the clamp. (2) ~180 DEG WHIP AT LAUNCH - the literal "not always in the right direction": Math.max(1.01, m*0.96) returns a value ABOVE m while m<1.01, reversing the chord and flipping atan2 to 239 deg instead of 59. Measured in Chrome as rot thrashing 57.7 -> 164.7 -> 106.5 -> 44.8 within the first 300ms. Fixed by clamping the chord tail strictly below m. RESULT over 42 samples m=1.03..4.63: mean |delta| 0.37 deg, worst 0.95 deg, "nose tracks the curve throughout". Deterministic check agrees: worst 0.91 deg over m=1.00..100.75 and frame-to-frame jump at launch now 0.00 deg (was ~180). Build exit 0, tsc clean. PROBE TRAP recorded for the next verifier: a "largest open SVG path" heuristic silently latches onto a DIFFERENT path for the first ~750ms (frozen pathLen 61.9) and reads as a bogus 73 deg rocket error - select the curve explicitly by stroke=url(#curveGradient). Aesthetic judgement in motion still unconfirmed by eye: image reads return "image not available" on this box.

FLAME TIP anchored to the trail line, per direct user observation while watching a live headed-Chrome flight: "the tip of the flame should be in the middle and over the moving line". Correct diagnosis - planePosition is where the CURVE is drawn, so whichever point of the artwork is placed there is the point that appears to touch the line, and both the offset translate(-50%,-75%) and transformOrigin center-75% used the BOX CENTRE. That put the rocket's middle on the line and left the flame tip ~16.2px off it at the shipped 45x80 size. Measured the flame tip from the asset the same way as the nose angle - flame pixels projected onto the nose axis, aft-most ~1.7% taken as the tip cluster, LATERAL CENTRE of that cluster so the tip is centred on the line rather than off one edge - giving 20.49%, 86.63% of the box. Both the translate offset AND the rotation origin now use that point, so the tip stays pinned at every angle instead of swinging off as the rocket lays over. VERIFIED in the live render across 14 samples m=1.02..2.72: gap between the flame tip and the stroked curve's end point is mean 0.0px, worst 0.1px. Build exit 0, tsc clean for AviatorGamePro. User confirmed everything else about the rocket reads correctly.

BLURRED LOGOS fixed - user reported "game logos are blurred". Root cause was OURS, not the assets: CrashPageSections.tsx GameArtCard painted a full-bleed overlay at inset-0 carrying backdropFilter blur 2.729px, and backdrop-filter blurs EVERYTHING rendered beneath it - so the whole game logo was frosted, not just the caption band the frame actually frosts. Compounding it, the img carried scale-110 even though the source art is 1163x1500 into a 195x277 box (a ~6x DOWNscale), so upscaling only threw the logo off its pixel grid. Fix: scope the frosted overlay to the bottom band (inset-x-0 bottom-0 top-41.8%, gradient rebased 0-63.4%) and drop scale-110. Measured after: every card image reports transform none, filter none, blurAncestor null, covering null - nothing blurs the art now. Both the game-info card and the More-games carousel share GameArtCard, so one fix covers both. Asset sizes audited and are NOT the problem (figma/*.webp all 1163x1500). Verified frame-verify exit 0.

(2) The frame's right-hand fiat readouts ($21.00 next to Balance, $1,376.97 next to Potential Profit) are NOT rendered — POINTS has no price and the widget holds no real quote for the active rail, so filling them would mean inventing a number. 768 TABLET PAGE — BUILT, and this is the frame the tablet tier follows. Measured off its own 768x1627 render rather than eyeballed: bet panel x150..617 = 468px CENTRED (page centre 384, panel centre 383.5), graph card x30..737 with a distinct fill (rgb 1,22,21) against the page's #001615. Implemented as `md:w-[468px] md:mx-auto` on the panel with the graph inset `md:px-[30px]`, both reverting at `lg` so the verified 356px desktop column is untouched. ★ THE TWO SMALL TIERS DISAGREE ON WHERE THE CTA GOES, so "below lg" could not be one rule: this frame puts the Bet CTA BETWEEN the Balance row and Auto Cashout, while all three 375 panel frames put it at the very TOP above the bet amount. The CTA, bet-amount and currency blocks therefore carry an `md:` override (CTA order-1 -> md:order-3, amount order-2 -> md:order-1, currency order-3 -> md:order-2); the pair/auto/bets/stats/tabs sequence is identical in both small tiers and needs none. Stacking already worked (the outer flex is `flex-col lg:flex-row` with explicit order on both children); what did not exist was the panel's width, centring, radius, the graph's inset and radius below `lg`, and the four controls that were hidden outright. Declared size in the frame title (768x1024) does not match the frame (768x1627). Practice-mode toggle drawn by the frame is omitted per the standing product call; the Blackjack sample rows in Community wins are a no-mock-data exclusion the page already handles with honest empty states. NOT render-verified in a browser; `partial`, not `match`.

768 "CRASH ALT" — DECLINED AS A RIVAL, NOT SKIPPED. It is a genuine SKAI Crash frame, but it is mutually exclusive with 9003-96041 and the two disagree on the numbers that matter at 768: measured off their own renders the bet panel is 422px wide here (x173..594) versus 468px there (x150..617), and this frame draws the graph on the BARE page colour where 96041 gives it a distinct card fill. Both centre the panel, so the conflict is only width plus graph treatment — and nothing in the file resolves it. 96041 was built because it is the primary (un-suffixed) frame and its graph treatment matches the already-verified desktop frame 9142-18315; building both is impossible in one layout. Needs a product call on which 768 page is canonical; the loser should be deleted or renamed so the next pass does not re-litigate it.
